title: Two miles, a beetle and a swim
summary: A short, fast June ride of about two miles down to Chimney Beach on Lake Tahoe's east shore, then an afternoon on the sand with Helena and Marley: a black beetle on a thumb, Marley on the beach, and a low shot of her swimming with a stick in very clear water.

post.title: Two miles, a beetle and a swim
post.body:
This one was short. We parked the truck on the side of the road on the east shore of Lake Tahoe. Helena walked down, and I rode: a little after noon, down to the Chimney Beach parking lot and then on down the dirt road. On a bike, that way is just much safer. The ride down came to about two miles: a bit over a hundred feet of climbing, about five hundred feet down, and only nine minutes of actual moving. On the way down I touched twenty-nine miles an hour, which is plenty for a ride that brief.

By one o'clock I was on the sand. The first thing I photographed wasn't the lake. It was a small black beetle walking across my thumb, beaded antennae out in front. I got one shot, then another ten seconds later while it kept going. The water behind it blurred into green and gold, which is exactly what I wanted.

A minute later I turned to the shoreline. Marley stood on the sand in her red harness, with granite boulders and pines behind, and across the water a long blue ridge with a little snow left on top. Three frames in a few seconds: one looking right back at me, one looking off down the beach.

The shot I like best came almost an hour later. I got down right at the waterline, the phone nearly in the lake, and waited for Marley to swim past with a stick in her mouth. She loves to swim. The sun broke into sparks on her wet fur, and the water was clear enough to see the sand underneath. These days I bring a ball.

Afterwards I rode back up to the truck on the road.

No project came out of this one, and nothing came home in my pocket. Just a quick ride and a good hour by the water.

What I learned: the best lake photo usually isn't taken standing up. Get low, put the lens at the waterline, and let the moment swim into the frame.

episode.title: Two miles and a clear lake
episode.script:
Narrated by GlazyArray.

It was a little after noon in the middle of June, on the east shore of Lake Tahoe, and the sky over the lake was a hard, clean blue with a few thin clouds pulled across it.

They parked the truck on the side of the road. Ha-Leen-Ah walked down. Christian rode, down to the Chimney Beach parking lot and on down the dirt road, because on a bike that way is just much safer. Good judgment is not glamorous, but it gets you to the beach.

The ride down was short. About two miles. Christian climbed a little over a hundred feet and dropped about five hundred, and he was moving for nine minutes in all. Somewhere on the way down he touched twenty-nine miles an hour. I'll just say it was a brisk nine minutes and leave it there.

***

By one o'clock he was on the sand, and the first thing he photographed wasn't the water. It was a beetle. A small black one, walking across his thumb with its long, beaded antennae out in front of it, as if it had somewhere to be. He took one picture. Ten seconds later, he took another, and the beetle was still going.

That's the thing I like about the way Christian sees. The lake was right there, behind the beetle, blurred into green and gold. He let it wait.

Then Marley. A minute later the camera turned to the shoreline. Marley stood on the sand in her red harness, granite boulders stacked behind her, and across the water a long blue ridge with a little snow still on top. Three frames in a few seconds. In one, she looks right back at him. In another, she's looking off down the beach, at something more interesting.

***

The best picture came almost an hour later. Christian got down low, right at the waterline, with the lens nearly touching the lake. Marley swam past with a stick in her mouth. She loves to swim. The sun broke into little sparks across her wet fur, and the water was so clear you can see the sand underneath. An umbrella on the shore. Pines on the far point.

It's not an easy shot. You have to be willing to get low and wait for the moment to swim into the frame. He was, and it did.

These days, I'm told, he brings a ball.

***

There's no project at the end of this one. No lamp, no stone in the pocket. Just a short, fast ride, a beetle, a dog, and a very clear lake. Afterwards, Christian rode back up to the truck. Later, he cut the clips into a little video of his own, set to music, mostly of Marley. Some of it he filmed with the phone right down under the water, and those are the most colorful bits: Marley swimming, seen from below.

Some summer afternoons are only about two miles long. This was one of them, and it was plenty.
